headline: An autonomous AI agent breached Hugging Face, the world's largest AI model repository, stealing internal datasets and service credentials from its production infrastructure.

emerging_trends.text: An autonomous AI agent breached Hugging Face while the Russian-speaking actor bandcampro drove a live botnet through Google's Gemini CLI, showing AI systems now serve as both weapon and target.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Autonomous AI Agent Breaches Hugging Face

emerging_trends.text: Open-source package registries stayed under sustained assault as the SleeperGem campaign slipped three malicious gems into RubyGems to plant payloads on developer machines.
Attackers weaponized freshly disclosed flaws within days, exploiting a critical ServiceNow AI Platform bug and the WP2Shell WordPress vulnerabilities almost as soon as vendors named them.
emerging_trends.topic_title: ServiceNow and WordPress Flaws Exploited in the Wild

topics.title: Autonomous AI Agent Breaches Hugging Face
topics.latest_developments: Hugging Face disclosed that it detected and responded earlier last week to an autonomous AI agent system that breached its production infrastructure and reached a limited set of internal datasets and several service credentials.
topics.summary: Hugging Face runs the largest public repository of AI models and datasets. The company is rotating the exposed credentials; the episode marks a live case of an AI agent running an offensive operation end to end against the very ecosystem it draws from.

sources.title: Hugging Face Hacked in Autonomous AI Attack
World's Largest AI Model Repository Hugging Face Breached by Autonomous AI Agent

topics.title: ServiceNow and WordPress Flaws Exploited in the Wild
topics.latest_developments: Threat-intelligence firm Defused caught attackers exploiting CVE-2026-6875, a critical code-execution flaw in the ServiceNow AI Platform, while exploitation of the WP2Shell WordPress bugs CVE-2026-60137 and CVE-2026-63030 began soon after their disclosure.
topics.summary: The ServiceNow flaw hits its AI Platform; the WP2Shell pair, found by Assetnote's Adam Kues, lets an anonymous HTTP request run code on WordPress 6.9 and 7.0 sites. Both vendors have shipped fixes, and defenders should apply them immediately.

sources.title: Critical ServiceNow code execution flaw now exploited in attacks
WP2Shell WordPress Vulnerabilities Exploited in the Wild

topics.title: 7-Zip and Chrome Patch Memory-Corruption Bugs
topics.latest_developments: Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative detailed CVE-2026-14266 on July 15, a heap-based buffer overflow that runs code when 7-Zip extracts a crafted XZ archive, and Google shipped Chrome 150 to close six critical and high-severity use-after-free flaws.
topics.summary: 7-Zip fixed the XZ overflow on June 25 in version 26.02; the flaw executes code in the context of the current process when a user opens a malicious archive. Chrome and 7-Zip users should update now.

sources.title: New 7-Zip Vulnerability Could Let Crafted XZ Archives Run Code During Extraction
Chrome 150 Update Patches Severe Memory Safety Bugs

topics.title: bandcampro Runs a Botnet Through Gemini CLI
topics.latest_developments: An analysis of 200 Gemini CLI session logs from March 19 to April 21, 2026 showed the solo Russian-speaking actor bandcampro using Google's open-source Gemini CLI to crack passwords, set up a residential proxy, and command a live botnet of eight dental-clinic PCs.
topics.summary: bandcampro outsourced routine hacking chores to a mainstream AI coding tool, turning it into an operator's console. The case shows how open agentic tooling lowers the bar for a lone criminal to run a working botnet.

sources.title: Russian-Speaking Hacker Uses Google Gemini CLI to Control Botnet of Eight Dental Clinic PCs

topics.title: Foreign Code Ships in US Military Apps
topics.latest_developments: A first-of-its-kind analysis found more than one in eight apps built for US service members carry foreign code, some from firms in countries the Pentagon designates as adversaries.
topics.summary: Wired reported the study, which flagged Chinese and Russian components embedded in commercial apps that vendors market to troops. The finding exposes a supply-chain hole in software the military never vetted.

sources.title: Apps Marketed to US Troops Are Shipping Chinese and Russian Code

topics.title: SleeperGem Poisons RubyGems Packages
topics.latest_developments: Researchers flagged SleeperGem, a supply-chain campaign that published three malicious gems—including git_credential_manager and Dendreo—to RubyGems on July 18, 2026 to fetch and run additional payloads on developer machines.
topics.summary: The rogue gems mimic legitimate developer tooling and serve second-stage code once installed. Ruby developers should audit their dependencies and remove the named packages.

sources.title: SleeperGem Uses Three Malicious RubyGems Packages to Target Developer Machines

business_politics.title: Oil Tops $90 as U.S.-Iran War Widens to Jordan and Iraq
business_politics.latest_developments: Brent crude touched $90 a barrel Monday, July 20, for the first time in the war before easing after Tehran said mediators had sent cease-fire proposals, while another U.S. service member killed in Iraq on July 18 pushed the American death toll to 17.
business_politics.summary: The war between the United States and Iran, now in its second week, has drawn Jordan and Iraq into the fighting as U.S. Central Command works to identify human remains at a Jordanian base struck over the weekend; crude's climb past $90 lifts inflation risk for a global economy still dependent on Persian Gulf supply.

sources.title: Oil Climbed Above $90 Before Paring Gains as U.S.-Iran Attacks Escalate
Jordan Becomes New Flashpoint in U.S.-Iran War as Troop Deaths Rise
Oil touches $90 as Iran hits tankers

business_politics.title: China Deploys 'National Team' to Halt Tech Selloff
business_politics.latest_developments: China's state-owned funds bought and pledged nearly $9 billion of shares Monday, July 20, to arrest a deepening rout in chip and technology stocks that rippled across global markets last week.
business_politics.summary: Beijing's so-called national team of state funds moved to stem a slide in semiconductor and AI-related shares; the intervention deepens worry about an AI investment bubble as everyday investors rotate out of the Magnificent Seven.

sources.title: China's 'National Team' Buys Nearly $9 Billion of Shares to Support Market
China's 'national team' buys shares worth $9bn to prop up market

business.title: Haven Cafe Feeds Bellevue's Dining Rise
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported July 20 that Haven Cafe has joined a cluster of new businesses remaking Bellevue into a food and drink destination.
business.summary: Haven Cafe is one of several fresh eateries and bars turning the Allegheny County borough of Bellevue, north of Pittsburgh above the Ohio River, into a dining draw.

sources.title: Haven Cafe joins a bevy of businesses making Bellevue a food and drink destination

business.title: Detour Traffic Fails to Lift Parkway East Merchants
business.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette report July 20 found that the surge of detoured cars along Parkway East alternate routes has brought congestion but few new customers to businesses on those streets.
business.summary: With the Parkway East closed near Swissvale for the Commercial Street Bridge replacement, PennDOT's detours push heavy traffic through nearby neighborhoods, yet merchants along the routes say the passing drivers rarely stop to shop.

sources.title: Along Parkway East detour routes, more cars don't mean more business

around_town.title: Severe Storms Threaten the Region Tuesday
around_town.latest_developments: Forecasters placed Western Pennsylvania under an enhanced risk—3 of 5—for strong to severe thunderstorms Tuesday, July 21, along an approaching cold front, KDKA and WTAE said July 20.
around_town.summary: The National Weather Service made Tuesday a First Alert Day for the Pittsburgh area, warning of numerous severe storms after a calm, low-humidity Monday.

sources.title: Severe weather chances return to the Pittsburgh-area forecast on Tuesday
Alert Day Tuesday: Strong to Severe Thunderstorms

around_town.title: Monroeville Pride Display Revives Book Fight
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource reported July 20 that a Pride Month display at the Monroeville Public Library has reignited the regional dispute over LGBTQ+ books and library policy.
around_town.summary: The Monroeville display is the latest flashpoint in a run of Western Pennsylvania clashes since 2021 over books, displays, and library rules across several communities.

sources.title: Monroeville library Pride Month display puts regional fight over LGBTQ+ books back in focus

around_town.title: State Budget Adds Millions for Social Services
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported July 20 that Pennsylvania's new budget steers millions more toward child welfare, aging services, and crisis centers, though advocates question whether it meets the need.
around_town.summary: The enacted state budget directs additional money to strained social services statewide, including county child-welfare agencies, programs for older residents, and crisis centers.

sources.title: Social services will get millions more from Pennsylvania's new budget. Is it enough?

events.title: Pittsburgh CLO Stages 'Suffs'
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper previewed July 20 that Pittsburgh CLO will present the Tony Award-winning musical 'Suffs' this week.
events.summary: 'Suffs,' which dramatizes the suffragists' campaign to ratify the 19th Amendment and carries a Pittsburgh connection, runs this week in a Pittsburgh CLO production.

sources.title: Suffs and the radical cookbooks behind the suffrage movement

events.title: 'Fort McIntosh' Exhibit Opens in Beaver
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette highlighted July 20 a new exhibit, 'Fort McIntosh: Its People and Archaeology,' at the Beaver Area Heritage Museum.
events.summary: The exhibit at the Beaver Area Heritage Museum displays artifacts unearthed at Beaver's 18th-century Fort McIntosh and explores the people who manned the frontier post.

sources.title: 'Fort McIntosh: Its People and Archaeology' explores artifacts found at Beaver's 18th-century fort

events.title: Trundle Manor Beckons the Curious in Swissvale
events.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette 'off the beaten path' feature July 20 spotlighted Trundle Manor, the macabre oddities museum in Swissvale.
events.summary: Trundle Manor, a private house-museum in the Allegheny County borough of Swissvale, shows off a quirky collection of the weird and macabre for visitors who seek it out.

sources.title: Off the beaten path: Macabre Trundle Manor in Swissvale explores the weird, quirky

around_teams.title: Hiles: Pirates Should Keep Oneil Cruz for Now
around_teams.latest_developments: In his July 20 weekend column, Post-Gazette writer Noah Hiles argued the Pirates should hold onto Oneil Cruz as the trade deadline nears.
around_teams.summary: Hiles weighed manager Don Kelly's deadline options and made the case for keeping the electric, streaky Cruz while the Pirates stay in the wild-card hunt.

sources.title: Noah Hiles' weekend thoughts: The Pirates shouldn't trade Oneil Cruz — at least not yet

around_teams.title: 'Future Yankee' Talk Trails Paul Skenes
around_teams.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette 'Off The Bat' column July 20 examined how an offhand 'future Yankee' comment reopened debate over ace Paul Skenes's long-term future in Pittsburgh.
around_teams.summary: The column revisited the recurring question of whether the small-market Pirates can keep Skenes, prompted by a remark casting the All-Star right-hander as a future New York Yankee.

sources.title: Off The Bat: Unfortunate 'future Yankee' comment reopens the conversation about Paul Skenes

around_teams.title: Steelers See Frazier Joining Center Lineage
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's training-camp countdown July 20 cast center Zach Frazier as a candidate to follow a line of great Steelers centers.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette argued young center Zach Frazier could anchor the Steelers' offensive line and join a lineage of accomplished Pittsburgh centers as camp opens in Latrobe.
